NOTE: This fix for Windows Updates applies only to Windows 7 (x86 or x64), and does not apply to Vista, Win8, Win8.1, or other flavors.

Step 1: Go into Windows Update settings and change it to "Never check for updates." Then restart your computer.

Step 2: Open Windows Powershell. Type the two following commands:

get-hotfix -id KB30202369

get-hotfix -id KB3172605

These two commands are to check if your system has these two particular hot-fixes installed on your system. If BOTH commands returned:

Source Description HotFixID InstalledBy InstalledOn
------ ----------- -------- ----------- -----------
< INFO ON THIS LINE>

Then this fix will NOT apply to you. If you are having Update issues then you have a larger issue at hand with your system -- what that issue maybe, I don't know as it could be a few different this.

IF one or both commands returns: 


get-hotfix : Cannot find the requested hotfix on the 'localhost' computer. Verify the input and run the command again.
At line:1 char:1
+ get-hotfix -id KB#######
+ ----------------------------------------
 + CategoryInfo : ObjectNotFound: (:) [Get-HotFix], ArgumentException
 + FullyQualifiedErrorId : GetHotFixNoEntriesFound,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.GetHotFixCommand

Then one or both of these updates are not yet installed on your system. Get the updates manually:

MS Support page for KB 3020369

MS Support page for KB 3172605

Step 3: Install missing updates downloaded from Step-2. NOTE: Run the updates in numerical order, and if it asks you to reboot system then reboot.

Step 4: Go back into Windows Update settings and re-enable Windows Updates to your personal perference.

Windows Updates should now find all your updates in the magnitude of 10-20 minutes. If you're still having updates issue then your system has other issues. Perhaps currupt update catalog or munged registry from virus or Malware - I can't say from this scope.

As for the other (older) flavors of Windows I haven't found a silver-bullet fix for them yet. My current workaround is to use: 3rd-party app: WindowsUpdatesDownloader

My cousin's husband Vladimir has a youtube channel called Invincible Extremes Muscle Car Garage. Vlad is an ex Army Sergeant and wants to move his family out to Hawaii where I live. To facilitate their transition he joined the National Guard here and flies out once a month. Well, one month, he comes up to me and says, "Mike, your car is missing half of an engine...you need a real car. There's one out in Kona for $500, Lets go get it."

So I scrape up some money and we drive out into the Kona desert to find this thing sitting on someone's property. No title. No keys. No clue what, if anything, was even wrong with it. I looked at Vlad and say, "Bro, the first time I ever got under a car was when I was 12yo and my father decided it was time for me to learn how to change the oil in his car, since then I've learned a few other tricks, but this is a little out of my league...you sure we can fix this thing up without bankrupting me?"

"Of course."

"Ok. Let's pull the trigger on it then." We spent the next week in 90F weather, under full sun, lying on dusty sharp rocks, trying to figure out how to get it started. Ultimately, after far too much cussing, we finally did, but it still wouldn't shift into gear, so we had to trailer it 90+miles back to my side of the island. Once we were back home, we tortured it (and ourselves) some more and finally got it to drive....ish. That became the first Surfin Bird video.

Right now, including the cost of the car, we are about $1,800 in, the car runs, drives, looks a little nicer (after many bottles of black spray paint), and even has a few upgrades which include a corvette 11" front disc brake upgrade and a used NASCAR AN-10 (5/8") fuel line. This fuel line is crazy big...after doing some math, it holds a whole quart of gasoline and we had to run it loooow so that the current fuel pump could have a chance of sucking up a bit of the 2lbs of gasoline a sip at a time while the weight of the gas in the fuel tank helps push a bit. We may have to upgrade the pump...or add a secondary electric push pump near the gas tank later....or we could also remove the professionally installed massive fuel filter...i guess.

Anyway, this is going to be a long term project, money don't grow on trees, but luckily Vlad agreed to put the ad revenue from the Surfin Bird videos towards parts for the Bird, so it would be nice if you guys watched a few videos. Hopefully they're entertaining enough and that way we both win. I'll be posting irregular updates here and there, but the videos for this car can be found here.

Anyway, aloha goats, and mahalo's for reading/watching.
